description:
Have you ever had a thought like one of these?
- “Because I feel there’s no point in trying for this promotion, now I’m not going to try.”
- “I think I’m socially awkward, so others don’t like talking to me.”
- “I feel like an imposter at work, so I’m incapable of succeeding in this role.”

Often, when we get stuck in a spiral of negative self-talk, we begin to conflate our thoughts with believability. In other words, “I had the thought, and so the thought must be true.” But when we accept all of our thoughts and feelings as facts, they can start to boss us around—causing us to move away, instead of toward, the things that would be most helpful.

One way we can elevate ourselves out of a negative self-talk spiral is to cognitively take on another perspective. So next time you have a challenging thought, ask yourself, “Who told you that?”
transcript: I wanna share with you one of the most powerful strategies when you are stuck in a spiral of negative self-talk. Ask yourself this, who told you that? I'm an imposter, who told you that? I'm unworthy, who told you that? There's no point in me trying this thing at work. Who told you that? When we have thoughts, sometimes we treat those thoughts as fact. In other words, we conflate the thought with the thought must be believable, it must be true. When we ask who told you that, you automatically create a sense of distance and separation. You start to observe your thought as a thought, not a fact. To be clear, this is not to deny reality. Rather, it is about not treating your thoughts as if they are immutable. And you might ask yourself, well, what if my parent told me I was unworthy? What if my boss told me that I wasn't good at the job? Again, asking yourself, who told you that, moves yourself into recognizing that the person who told you that is a person with an opinion and what you are hearing is their opinion. Again, it is not a fact. So next time you have a difficult thought, have fun with who told you that. Who told you that? Your dog? Did your dog tell you that? Did Spongebob tell you that? Did Donald Duck tell you that? Who told you that?
